sourceRef.section: 7. Mission Actions — 8. Scoring and Timing Clarifications

missionActions.overview: Certain Missions permit interactions called Mission Actions. A Unit may make at most one Mission Action per Round, in either its Movement activation or its Assault activation. A Mission Action completely replaces the Unit's ordinary action in that selected phase; it does not replace Commands and does not consume CP unless a particular mission says otherwise.

byPhase.rule: Select an eligible Unit for Movement activation; perform the legal interaction instead of moving, Disengaging, or taking another ordinary Movement action during that activation. It may still perform a legal ordinary Assault action later in the Round.

Select an eligible Unit for Assault activation; perform the interaction instead of Assault Moving, attacking, or charging. It cannot combine the interaction with any other ordinary Assault action in the same activation.
No ordinary Mission Actions. Combat activations belong to eligible Engaged Units, and Mission Actions do not occur in Combat.

generalRules: Unless a Mission states otherwise, the Unit must be unengaged, have at least one eligible Model within 1" of the object or objective, and satisfy any interaction restriction.
Withdrawn Units cannot perform Assault Mission Actions.
Mission Actions are not Attacks and do not automatically require Skill checks.

A Unit may perform ordinary eligible Commands with normal timing and CP cost during its activation unless a specific ability says otherwise. A Command never grants an additional ordinary action implicitly.
missionActions.characterSkillAlternatives: An explicit mission may allow an eligible Character to attempt an interaction through a Movement-phase Skill Action costing 1 CP; this replaces that Character's ordinary Movement action and uses the mission's stated Difficulty (Normal / 2 successes unless specified). The Character must still be in legal interaction range unless the mission expressly grants a remote action. A Character cannot count an interaction twice by using both its Skill Alternative and an ordinary Mission Action in the same Round.

scoringAndTimingClarifications.previousRoundControl: When a Mission compares objective control with the previous Round, record objective control at the end of every Scoring Phase, including Round 1.
scoringAndTimingClarifications.simultaneousScoring: Both players determine Primary and Tactical VP for the same Scoring Phase before checking for Decisive Victory.
scoringAndTimingClarifications.multipleObjectives: A Unit may contribute to only one objective's control during the same Scoring Phase. A single Unit may nevertheless carry a Relic or possess another scenario token while controlling an eligible objective, provided it is not Withdrawn or otherwise ineligible.
scoringAndTimingClarifications.tokensAndScenarioObjects: Scenario tokens and markers do not block Model movement unless their specific rules say otherwise. A dropped object should be represented by a flat marker where practical.
